description:
A 27B-parameter LLM running on an iPhone, fully offline, at 1 bit per weight. Here's how Bonsai 27B fits a dense model into under 4 GB, and exactly what breaks when you do it.

Running a large language model on a phone used to be impossible: the full-precision model needs 54 GB, and iOS hands a single app only about 6. This video breaks down how extreme quantization crushes 27 billion parameters into a 1-bit build small enough to run on-device, why it doesn't fall apart, and where the missing 10% actually hides. We map the real trade-offs across math, coding, and agentic tool use, plus the speed and battery numbers on real hardware.

CHAPTERS
00:00 The 27B model that runs on a phone
00:36 Why the full model needs 54 GB
01:39 What 1 bit per weight actually means
02:59 Why the model doesn't collapse (quantization-aware training)
04:16 Miracle or lobotomy: what breaks first
05:50 Speed and battery on real hardware
06:43 Phone vs datacenter: two ends of one curve
07:32 Breakthrough or overhyped?

What is 1-bit quantization? Quantization stores each model weight with fewer bits to shrink the model. Standard builds use 4 or 8 bits. A 1-bit build keeps only the sign of each weight (plus or minus), with one shared scale per block, so a 27B model that normally needs 54 GB can run locally on a phone. It works without collapsing because the model is retrained with the constraint switched on, so it learns to route around the missing precision. That is the difference between a local LLM you can actually use offline and one that loops on the first hard task.

WHAT THIS VIDEO COVERS
- How a dense 27B model gets from 54 GB down to under 4 GB
- The phone memory ceiling that makes on-device LLMs so hard
- Why 1 bit per weight is really 1.125 bits, and why quant labels lie
- Quantization-aware training vs native 1-bit pretraining like BitNet
- 4-bit KV cache and packed-bit kernels that keep it fast
- What degrades: agentic tool calling, instruction following, non-English
- The kernel trap that makes a 1-bit model run slower than a 4-bit one
- Speed, battery life, and the honest use cases for a local LLM
